# landing/ — marketing page

A static page: React 18 UMD with in-browser Babel, and no build step. Preview it with the `landing` entry in `.claude/launch.json`.

- **Every claim must match what the code does today.** Don't add accuracy, latency or throughput figures, and don't describe a live mode as shipped. The owner chose facts over marketing numbers.
- **`app/data.js` is real pipeline data.** `export_data.py` generates it; run `ai/.venv/bin/python landing/export_data.py` from the repo root. Never hand-edit it. It holds keypoints only and no video frames, because the fight footage isn't ours to publish.
- **Red and blue always mean corners, and orange is only the brand and CTA colour**, so a strike mark never reads as a corner. Corner blue here is `#4f93ea`, not the app's `#60a5fa`, because the lighter blue fails the dataviz lightness band on this dark surface.
- **Upload is admin-only in the backend**, so the page's only call to action is signing in, not uploading.
- **Each scroll moves exactly one section.** With a mouse, trackpad or keyboard, `app/pager.js` handles it and CSS snapping stays off. On touch screens, native mandatory snapping handles it. Both read their stops from each element's `scroll-snap-align` in `app/site.css`, so a new section needs one; without it, both paths jump straight past the section.
- **Analytics is Umami Cloud's free plan and must stay cookieless.** The owner won't show a consent banner, so never add GA, Clarity, session replay or anything else that sets cookies. Each stored event property counts against the monthly event cap, so keep properties to one per event. The website ID is in `index.html`, and the script doesn't load on localhost.

content.text:
I've fixed all three problems in the hero replay (the "first animation"). Both changes are in [stage.jsx](landing/app/stage.jsx). I checked frames from the start, middle and end of the loop, plus the Pose layer, and there are no console errors. Nothing is committed.

**What was wrong:** the drawing code skips any bone whose joint the pose model is less than 30% sure of.
- **Blue's leg:** the model has no detection of blue in 7 of the last 8 samples, and the one it does have places the leg joints badly. So the leg vanished and the pose froze at the end.
- **Red's left hand:** red's left elbow and wrist keep dropping below the 30% cutoff, especially near the end.
- **Red's head:** the head circle's size came from shoulder width in each frame. When a fighter turns side-on, that width shrinks from about 100 px to 5 px, so the head grew and shrank. Its centre also jumped whenever a face point crossed the cutoff.

**What changed:**
- **The loop now ends at the last sample where both fighters are detected** (sample 102 of 110). Every strike in the clip happens before that, so none are lost. Because of this, I changed the caption from "4.4 seconds" to "3.7 seconds" so it matches what plays.
- **Missing limb joints are filled in:** when the model loses an elbow, wrist, knee or ankle for up to 1 second, the joint stays attached to its parent joint. Its angle and length are blended from the frames on either side of the gap, so a limb stays the right length and doesn't fly off. This also fills red's ankles at the start of the loop, which are cut off by the edge of the broadcast frame.
- **The head size now comes from torso length,** which doesn't shrink when a fighter turns. I smoothed it over time, and the head centre now weights each face point by how sure the model is of it, so it no longer jumps.
- **The Pose layer still shows the model's own uncertainty:** its "hollow points are unsure joints" view uses the unfilled data, so the filled-in joints don't hide it.

One leftover that comes from the data itself: during blue's middle kick (around sample 27), the model is fairly sure of a knee position that's wrong, so that leg snaps briefly. My fix only touches joints below the cutoff, so it doesn't catch this.
Also when page is in the mobile mode, animations also break and mix up when scrolling the page. It is not smooth enough for mobile devices.

content.text:
I've fixed the mobile replay: it now shows the layer that matches the section on screen, and its canvas no longer resizes while you scroll. I checked it in the preview at phone size (375×812) and on desktop, but not on a real phone or with real touch momentum. Nothing is committed.

**What was wrong on mobile:**
- **The replay got stuck on the wrong layer.** It only changed layer when a section's text crossed a thin strip low on the screen, and nothing reset it after that. So a quick flick could skip a section, and scrolling back up to the top still left "Timeline" showing over the hero.
- **The canvas resized while you scrolled, which made it jerky.**
  - Changing layer folds the strike log away over about half a second, which made the canvas resize on every frame of that time. Each resize rebuilds the canvas and changes the fighters' scale.
  - The replay's height and the section heights were tied to the visible screen height (CSS `dvh`). On a phone that changes as the browser's address bar slides in and out, so the canvas also resized mid-scroll and the snap points moved.

**What changed:**
- **The layer is now worked out from the scroll position on every scroll,** so it always matches whatever section is on screen, in both directions. The change is in [app.jsx](landing/app/app.jsx).
- **On phones, sizes use `svh` instead of `dvh`,** which stays fixed when the address bar moves. The strike log also keeps its space and fades out instead of folding away. In my check the canvas stayed at one size through every layer change. These changes are in [site.css](landing/app/site.css).
- **Two smaller fixes in [stage.jsx](landing/app/stage.jsx):**
  - The canvas is only rebuilt when its size really changes.
  - If you scroll past the Pose section before the replay has finished settling into the held pose, the fight now carries on from where it stopped. Before, it jumped to a different frame.

On phones, the Pose, Corners and Strikes layers now leave an empty strip where the log would be. That's the trade-off for not resizing the canvas.

I also added two short notes to [landing/CLAUDE.md](landing/CLAUDE.md). One is about this canvas-size rule. The other is that a plain reload in the preview can run old cached `.jsx` files, which fooled my first round of checks here.

content.text:
I've fixed this: on phones, each step now stops with its title just below the player. I checked it in the preview at 375×667 and 390×844, but not on a real phone with real touch scrolling. Nothing is committed.

**Why titles were hidden:** each step's text sat at the bottom of its section, and the page snapped that section's bottom edge to the bottom of the screen. On a phone around 667 px tall, the text is taller than the space left under the player, so the title ended up 60–120 px underneath it.

**What changed:**
- **Snap point ([site.css](landing/app/site.css)):** on phones, each step now snaps by its top, just under the pinned player. Each step fills exactly the space left below the player, so the next step's title stays off-screen until you swipe.
- **Player height ([app.jsx](landing/app/app.jsx)):** the page measures the player's height and passes it to the CSS. If the player's height changes, the snap point follows it. Which layer is active is now judged against the space under the player, not a fixed spot on the screen.
- **Short phones:** the canvas shrinks first, down to 150 px, so the Strikes step's type and target chips still fit.
- **Mouse scrolling ([pager.js](landing/app/pager.js)):** the code that moves one section per wheel or key press now uses the same snap point, so a narrow desktop window lands in the same place.

Measured where the page comes to rest:

| Viewport | Player ends | Title starts | Text ends | Next title |

content.text:
I've fixed the cut-off title. Each step now fits on one screen, so the page always comes to rest with the title just below the player. I checked this in the preview at 408×747 and four other phone sizes, but not on a real device. Nothing is committed.

**Cause:** on your screen, the Strikes step was 715 px tall but only 691 px fits under the nav. When a step is taller than the screen, the browser is allowed to stop scrolling anywhere within that extra height. Here that let it stop up to 24 px lower, pushing the title under the player — that's what your screenshot shows. My previous check only scrolled to the exact snap point, so it missed this.

**What changed:**
- **[site.css](landing/app/site.css):**
  - Each step is now exactly one screen tall and snaps by its top edge.
  - The space for the player is now padding at the top of each step, instead of the earlier offset trick that made neighbouring steps' snap areas overlap.
  - I removed the bottom padding, and on very short phones the canvas can shrink to 120 px so the Strikes step still fits.
- **[pager.js](landing/app/pager.js):** the mouse/trackpad scroll handler now steps aside whenever the page is in touch mode. Before, it decided once at page load, so turning on DevTools device mode afterwards left it fighting the browser's own snapping.
- **[landing/CLAUDE.md](landing/CLAUDE.md):** added a note that each step must fit on one screen on phones.

To test it, I scrolled 25 px past each snap point and checked where the page settled:

| Viewport | Tallest step | Drift after scroll | Player ends | Title starts |

| 360×640 | 584 / 584 | 0 | 330 | 350 |
| 375×667 | 611 / 611 | 0 | 360 | 380 |
| 390×844 | fits | 0 | 463 | 477 |
| 408×747 (yours) | 691 / 691 | 0 | 434 | 454 |

- On a 640 px tall phone the fighters are drawn quite small, because the canvas is only 120 px tall.
- A 320 px wide phone (the original iPhone SE) still won't fit the Strikes step, so the title could slip under the player there.

content.text:
I've redesigned the mobile "How it works" section so the text can no longer end up under the player. I checked it in the preview at 408×747 and 360×640, measured the player header from 320 to 430 px wide, and checked desktop. It isn't tested on a real phone, and nothing is committed.

The old design was the problem: it kept the player pinned to the top while the text scrolled underneath it, and only worked if each swipe stopped at an exact pixel. In DevTools with a mouse wheel it often didn't, which is what your screenshots show.

**The new mobile layout ([app.jsx](landing/app/app.jsx), [site.css](landing/app/site.css)):**
- **Player inline:** the player is no longer pinned; it scrolls with the page like any other block.
- **Tappable layers:** Pose, Corners, Strikes and Timeline in the player's header are now buttons that switch the layer.
- **Text below:** the selected step's title and text sit underneath, with a "2 / 4 · Next: Strikes →" row, and "Start again" on the last step.
- **Steady height:** the text area is always as tall as the longest step. Switching layers didn't move the page in my checks.

**Smaller fixes along the way:**
- The player's header was too wide at 360 px and cut off the play button. I tightened its spacing, and below 340 px wide the frame number is hidden.
- When switching steps, the old text now disappears at once instead of fading out on top of the new text.
- The "Start again" icon had shown as the word "REPLAY", because that icon wasn't in the icon font request in [index.html](landing/index.html).

Desktop keeps the scroll-driven layout with the pinned player.

A few things worth knowing:
- **One wording change:** "Try it: click a row in the log" now says "pick a row", since it applies to taps too. It changed on desktop as well.
- **Blank strip:** on the Pose, Corners and Strikes layers, the empty space where the log would be is still kept, so the canvas doesn't resize when you switch layers.
- **Hard reload:** in DevTools, hard-reload the page before testing. Your browser may still be holding the old cached files.

content.text:
I've fixed it: the mobile layout now scrolls freely, even when DevTools isn't emulating touch. I tested it in my preview browser, not in Brave itself.

**Cause:** in DevTools' Responsive mode without touch emulation, the browser still reports a mouse and no touch screen. So the mouse/trackpad scroll handler in [pager.js](landing/app/pager.js) kept running on the mobile layout and jumped a whole section on every wheel tick. That's the "snapping" you saw. I reproduced it here at 850×800 with no touch: one wheel tick jumped from 0 to 278 px, straight to the next section.

**Fix:** that handler now stays off whenever the mobile layout is showing (up to 899 px wide), as well as on touch screens. It checks on every scroll, so turning on device mode or resizing the window after the page has loaded also counts.

**Result in the preview:**
- At 850×800 with no touch, each wheel tick now scrolls a normal 100 px (0 → 100 → 200).
- At 1200×800, desktop still moves one section per tick (0 → 736, the first step), and there are no console errors.

I also updated the scrolling note in [landing/CLAUDE.md](landing/CLAUDE.md).

In Brave, do a hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac) so it picks up the new `pager.js` instead of a cached copy.

content.text:
I've switched mobile back to the scroll-driven version: there are no buttons, and the replay changes layer as you scroll. I checked it in the preview from 320 to 408 px wide and on desktop, but not in Brave or on a real phone. Nothing is committed.

**How it works now:**
- **Pinned player:** the player stays pinned under the nav, and the step texts scroll up beneath it.
- **Layer switching:** the layer changes when a step's title rises past the middle of the space below the player. It's recalculated on every scroll, so scrolling back up resets it too: at the top it shows the full replay.
- **No snapping:** phones scroll freely, which is why this version now works where the earlier pinned design didn't.
- **One screen per step:** each step is at least as tall as the space below the player, with its text at the top. Wherever you stop on a step, its text sits below the player.

The tap buttons, the Next/Start again row and the extra icon are gone. The log hint reads "click a row" again.

**Checked in the preview:**
- At your 408×747 size, scrolling through the steps switched the layers to Pose, Strikes and Timeline, and back to the full replay at the top. (I spot-checked three of the four steps; Corners wasn't checked on its own.)
- At 360×640, 375×667, 390×844 and 408×747, each step's title sits just under the player and the whole step fits on screen. At 408×747 the next title also stays below the bottom edge.
- Desktop still moves one section per wheel tick. There are no console errors.

Two things to know:
- **While you're scrolling**, text passes under the player, the same way content passes under a pinned header.
- **On the smallest phones (320×568, the original iPhone SE)**, a step's text is taller than the space below the player. You'd need to scroll a bit further, and the title slides under the player while you read the rest.

The scrolling note in [landing/CLAUDE.md](landing/CLAUDE.md) is updated. In Brave, hard-reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) to pick up the new files.
